one_liner: Senior staff officer at DIA headquarters who advises agency leadership, briefs senior audiences, and coordinates strategy and messaging across the organization.
fit_summary: GG-14 is a senior grade that expects a year of GG-13-level staff or advisory work plus the ability to obtain a TS/SCI clearance. Daniel's resume shows support-level operations and no clearance, so he is unlikely to qualify.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring paths include public, veterans, federal excepted service, and National Guard), and all applicants must be U.S. citizens.
Requires eligibility for a Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) clearance, a security investigation, and a drug test.
Specialized experience and education requirements are not in the USAJOBS text. Check the full announcement on DIA's own careers site using the 6-digit Job Opening ID.
GG-14 normally requires about one year of experience equivalent to the next-lower (GG-13/GS-13) level. Confirm the exact standard in DIA's announcement.
keywords: large diverse internal and external audiences
strategy: Apply through DIA's online application system, not just USAJOBS. Find the posting by title and Job Opening ID, and read the full duties and qualifications before writing anything.

Answer the five assessment factors one by one, each with a concrete IEM example, such as facilitating exercises for federal, state and private-sector clients, helping counties update COVID-19 grant applications, or organizing FEMA Public Assistance onboarding data for decision makers.
Frame your IEM work in terms of client-facing advisory roles, stakeholder management, and briefing products, using only duties you actually performed. Note full-time hours and dates.
Keep the resume to two pages, and quantify the scope of your audiences and clients (agency level, size, seniority) where accurate.
Submit before November 6, 2026. Because GG-14 is a reach, also apply to DIA or other intelligence community staff roles at GG-11/12/13 that list the same assessment factors.
resume_bullets: Kept minutes at a large travel company's weekly meetings (Feb – Aug 2024).
Led a Simulation Cell unit at FEMA full-scale exercises two years in a row.
interview_questions: Tell us about a time you briefed senior leaders on a controversial or complex topic. How did you tailor the message?
How have you built and maintained a partnership with a senior stakeholder who disagreed with your recommendation?
Describe a time you turned a broad leadership goal into clear direction for a staff or team.
How would you get up to speed on DIA's mission and policies to give useful decision support?
watch_outs: You need to be able to obtain an SCI clearance, and the investigation can take many months; the posting also requires a drug test.
GG-14 is a senior grade, and his resume shows no senior-level staff or advisory experience.
There is no telework or remote option, so you would commute full-time from Manassas to Washington, DC.
The application window is short, running only October 23 to November 6, 2026.
